_README: MARKER-ONLY. Never shipped to the student before a teacher/marker PDF is actually generated. English-only, never translated. See CLAUDE.md §5.

markingScheme.criterion: Describes what they did and what happened (for example turned the gas peaker down, pumped or saved water, built a plant; frequency fell when supply was short and rose when supply was in surplus), quoting at least two of their own logged readings from the Investigation Record.
markingScheme.accept: Any two genuine logged values such as demand, supply or frequency (for example demand 305 MW, supply 270 MW, 59.88 Hz); approximate values and wording are fine.
markingScheme.insufficient: A general claim ('I kept it balanced') with no readings quoted from the Record.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why supply must match demand: if supply is less than demand the frequency falls below 60 Hz, if supply exceeds demand the frequency rises, so the grid must be balanced at every moment (using storage, gas, batteries or by changing plants).
markingScheme.accept: Any equivalent wording linking a supply shortfall to a falling frequency (or a surplus to a rising frequency) and the need to balance continuously.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying only that frequency 'went up and down' with no link to supply and demand.

markingScheme.criterion: States clearly whether the evidence supported or contradicted the hypothesis made in the Hypothesis stage, and why, using the readings or the outcome of the mission.
markingScheme.insufficient: Restating the hypothesis without judging it against the evidence.

markingScheme.criterion: States the First Law of Thermodynamics idea: energy is conserved, not destroyed, so the energy that is not turned into electricity leaves as heat (and reflected light); primary energy in equals electricity out plus heat lost.
markingScheme.accept: Any equivalent phrasing: energy cannot be created or destroyed, only converted; the 'lost' energy becomes waste heat.
markingScheme.insufficient: Saying the energy is 'lost' or 'wasted' with no mention that it is conserved and becomes heat.

markingScheme.criterion: Supports the answer with an efficiency or heat-loss figure from the simulation (for example solar is about 23% efficient so about 77% leaves as heat; gas peaker about 38%; battery about 91%; pumped hydro about 82%), or a figure read from the First Law panel.
markingScheme.accept: Any correct efficiency from the simulation, or heat-loss MW taken from the First Law panel; approximate figures are fine.
markingScheme.insufficient: A figure that is not linked to a plant or to heat loss.

markingScheme.criterion: Explains why the town still needs storage: solar only generates in daylight (and less under cloud) while demand peaks in the evening, so energy must be stored when there is surplus and released after sunset, otherwise supply would fall short and the frequency would drop.
markingScheme.accept: Any equivalent wording about the timing mismatch between solar output and the evening demand peak, and storage moving energy in time.
markingScheme.insufficient: A vague statement ('batteries are good') with no link to day/night or to the demand peak.

Describes what they did and what happened quoting at least two of their own logged readings, explains that a shortfall lowers and a surplus raises the frequency so supply must match demand, and states whether the evidence supported the hypothesis — all three analytic points present.

criteria.source: Assessed holistically across both the Explain and Apply answers together — independent of, and never overlapping with, the content marks above.

levels.descriptor: Too unclear or incomplete for the reasoning to be followed reliably.
Main meaning understandable, but organisation, precision or scientific vocabulary has problems.
Clear and logical, uses appropriate vocabulary (primary, secondary, efficiency, heat, conserved, frequency, storage, demand), precise enough to follow easily.

markingInstructions: Mark ONLY the two constructed responses (Explain, Apply), using each question's point-by-point markingScheme above (award each point independently unless it states a dependsOn, in which case only award it if the point it depends on was also awarded) and the rubric's level descriptors, which restate the same points as bands — do not invent extra criteria beyond what is defined here. Each rubric row's 'source' states exactly which question's marks it equals; never award a criterion's marks a second time on top of the question-level marks they restate. Copy auto_marked_score into knowledge_accuracy (6 marks). Accept scientifically valid alternative wording per each point's 'accept' field; do not penalise spelling or grammar unless it actually interferes with meaning. Use the raw Investigation Record data (the mission snapshot rows: demand, supply, clean share, frequency, efficiency, cash) to verify any claim the student makes about their own readings. Report total, percentage, one strength, one correction, one next step, under 80 words.
